stories.title: US elections: Progressive Democrat scores shock win in Florida
stories.summary: Voters headed to the polls in three US states on Tuesday for a series of Democratic and Republican primaries. The verdict in Alaska, Florida, and Wyoming testified to a Democratic Party split along establishment lines and progressives critical of US support for Israel and the war on Iran. The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac) played a key role in several races. Aipac showered funds on candidates on both sides of the aisle to defeat opponents critical of the US's interventions in the Middle East. Meanwhile, some challengers sought to tie voters' concerns about the cost of living to the cost of the US-Israeli war on Iran. Overall, the results underscored the establishment's hold on the states. In Florida, State Representative Angie Nixon, a Democratic Socialist and former union organiser, defeated Alexander Vindman, a retired army lieutenant colonel and national security council aide, in the Democratic primary race for governor. The margin and the financial disparity were formidable, as Nixon raised less than $1m, while Vindman raised more than $16m. Nixon's campaign emphasised an anti-war stance alongside Medicare for All and affordable housing. On the Republican side, Congressman Bryon Donalds won the primary against a field of candidates. Donalds was endorsed by US President Donald Trump and came under intense criticism from challenger James Fishback for his closeness to Aipac. Fishback, who was endorsed by far-right podcaster Nick Fuentes, campaigned critically against US support for Israel and the war on Iran.

stories.title: US gross national debt tops $40tn for first time
stories.summary: Rising costs of social safety-net programs, military and Trump’s tax cuts strain federal government budgets The US gross national debt pile has topped $40tn ⁠for the first time, the treasury department said on Wednesday, in another troubling milestone in the wake of decades of borrowing to fund government spending. As the rising costs of social safety-net programs, the military and Donald Trump’s tax cuts strain US federal government budgets, the treasury’s daily cash and debt balances statement showed total public debt outstanding at $40.047tn on Tuesday – a disclosure likely to escalate fears of a brewing fiscal crisis.
